output.brief: The remote promotion gap is mostly a tenure effect, not proximity bias. Remote staff are much newer: 215 of 340 started since March 2025, and only 32% are eligible for promotion (18+ months in level), versus 74% of office staff. Among eligible employees, remote and office rates are nearly identical (20.0% vs 21.1%), and nomination and approval rates are similar too. Remote attrition is not higher than office attrition. So the COO's diagnosis is not supported, and the attendance rule would penalise people who are simply new and would not have been eligible anyway. Confidence is moderate: the eligible-group gap of about one point rests on 110 remote staff, so a modest true difference cannot be ruled out. Stretch-assignment access was not measured, so it remains an open question. Next steps: do not announce the attendance rule; report promotion rates for eligible employees only, re-check at the FY2027 cycle, and check stretch-assignment access by arrangement before drawing conclusions about it. Briefings on eligibility rules may help, since remote staff are less sure how to progress.
